Arun Bhardwaj Presiding Officer: Motor Accident Claims Tribunalii, Dwarka Courts: New Delhi Mact No. 66/11/10 In The Matter Of : Rahul Jangid (aged about 13 years) Through his father Shri Ashok Jangid, R/o B149, Sector - 7, Pocket - 2, Dwarka, New Delhi 110075 ... Petitioner Versus 1. Prince Lawrence Dhyrianathan R/o B304, Dwarka Appt., Plot no. 21, Sec.7 Dwarka, Bijwasan S.O. South West Delhi - 110075. 2. Cholamandlam Insurance Co. Ltd. Nehru Place Branch Nehru Place, New Delhi ... Respondents Filed On : 09.07.2010 Reserved On : 28.01.2013 Decided On : 30.01.2013 J U D G M E N T : 1. This is a claim petition filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. 2. Respondent no.1 is the drivercumowner and Respondent no. 2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 3. It is stated in this claim petition that on 02.05.2009, applicant was travelling alongwith his father on a motorbike bearing registration no. DL9SAA1799.
texts.facts: This is a claim petition filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. 2. Respondent no.1 is the drivercumowner and Respondent no. 2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 3. It is stated in this claim petition that on 02.05.2009, applicant was travelling alongwith his father on a motorbike bearing registration no. DL9SAA1799. His father was driving the motorbike following all traffic rules and regulations, carefully, in his own lane and at a low speed and was coming from CITI Mall to his home. 5. However, when the applicant reached opposite Meghdoot Apartments, Sector 7, Dwarka near Ramphal Chowk, a car of make Ford Ikon, bearing registration no. DL3CAN0348, was parked in a stationary position on the left side of the road. 6. When the motor bike on which applicant was travelling with his father reached near above said car, Respondent no.1/driver of the Car suddenly, without taking any due precaution or caring for the safety of other commuters on the road, opened the driver's door in full swing and sudden and abrupt opening of the door by Respondent no.1 put the life and safety of applicant and his father in extreme danger. 7. It is stated that the applicant's father tried hard to stop the motorbike and navigate the same to safety but due to sudden and abrupt opening of the door of the car, he could not manage to avert the impact and ultimately the same resulted in collision of left edge of the handle of the bike with the car and as a result of this both the applicant as well as his father fell down from their motorbike on the road. 8. It is stated that after the accident, father of the applicant got up as he escaped the accident with minor injuries but found petitioner in despairing and unbearable pain. 9. Respondent No. 1 helped father of the claimant in taking claimant in his car to Ayushman Hospital where he left them and drove away from the hospital. 10. It is stated that on preliminary investigation it was diagnosed that applicant has suffered pelvic fracture and urethral injury. 11. On catheterisation, applicant did not void urine and was provided with supra pubic catheter. 12. It is stated that applicant remained on bed without any movement for two weeks with traction on both the legs with weights. 13. It is stated that the applicant was also admitted in Sir Ganga Ram Hospital on 7.6.2009 to be operated upon on 8.6.2009 but the treating doctor informed that applicant could not be operated upon as gap of strictures was found too big and there was no expectation of a good result by conducting such an operation. 14. It is stated that applicant was given treatment by way of cystoscopy and was discharged thereafter. 15. It is further stated that on 12.6.2009, applicant's parents went to Safdarjang Hospital, New Delhi where HOD Urology Dr. N.K.Mohanty advised for an open surgery (Urethroplasty) operation without any surety of 100% success. Date of admission was given by the HOD on 15.1.2010 i.e. after Rahul Jangid (Aged About 13 Years) vs Prince Lawrence Dhyrianathan on 30 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49828600/ 2 more than 7 months. 16. It is stated that in this period claimant remained under immense pain and to curtail waiting period, claimant approached Urology department, AIIMS where he was admitted on 23.9.2009 and the surgeon, instead of carrying out open operation, decided to go for endoscopic evaluation and did a laser operation under general anesthesia. The gap of stricture was evaluated at 33.5cm which is stated to be a big gap. 17. It is stated that claimant was discharged from AIIMS on 29.9.2009 and at that time, two catheters were in situ. 18. Again, on 26.11.09, claimant was admitted in AIIMS for endoscopic evaluation under general anesthesia and was discharged on 1.12.2009. 19. On 19.12.2009, the PUC was also removed with directions to report to the hospital immediately, if do not void. 20. The procedure of dilation was taught to applicant and his father. 21. At that time, the applicant was advised to dilate once a day but the very next day the urine stopped. 22. The claimant again approached the treating doctor who managed to insert catheter of lower number (10Fr) whereas the doctors had advised 14 Fr Catheter. 23. It is stated that since then the applicant is surviving by taking dilatation 23 times and sometimes 4 times a day also. 24. It is stated that dilatation 24 times a day results in burning, pain, irritation, itching and applicant is living a disabled life and is completely dependant on his parents. 25. In these circumstances, petitioner has claimed a compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ with interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing of this claim petition till its realization. 26. Respondent No. 1 has filed his written statement stating therein that the offending vehicle was a tractor which had hit the petitioner which was coming behind their scooter. Respondent no. 1 is falsely implicated in this accident because neither the petitioner nor the police could trace the offending vehicle tractor which had hit the petitioner. 27. Respondent No. 1 denied all other allegations made against him in claim petition and also stated that the vehicle in question is insured with Respondent No. 2 vide policy no. 3362/00333403/000/00, cover note no. 7409062 issued on 12.2.2009 and valid from 8th February 2009 to mid night 7th February, 2010. Respondent No. 2 also stated that the claim petition is bad for nonjoinder of parties. Petitioner's father who was driving the motorcycle was equally responsible for the accident and therefore, it is a case of composite negligence. 29. Rest of the contents of the claim petition were also denied. OPP 3) Relief. 31. Father of the petitioner entered in the witness box as PW1 and stated in his evidence by way of affidavit similar facts as were already stated by claimant in the claim petition. 32. Discharge card of Ayushman Hospital was proved as Ex. PW1/1, discharge summary of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital as Ex. PW1/2, discharge summary of AIIMS as Ex. PW1/3, discharge summary of AIIMS where he was admitted second time as Ex. PW1/4, treatment card at Ayushman Hospital as Ex. PW1/5, treatment card at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital as Ex. PW1/6, treatment record at Safdarjang Hospital as Ex. PW1/7 and other treatment record of the petitioner was proved as Ex. PW1/822, certificate given by Professor P.N. Dogra, Professor and Head AIIMS as Ex. PW1/23, blood bank and school record as Ex. PW1/24 and 25 and receipts for purchase of medicines as Ex. PW1/2653. 33. In cross examination, PW1 deposed that he has a driving license which was proved as Ex. PW1/DX. 34. He denied a suggestion that claimant was not wearing helmet at the time of accident or the accident has taken place due to negligence of PW1 himself. 35. He deposed that Respondent No. 1 had suddenly opened the driver's door of the car without looking for the traffic coming from its right side which resulted in the accident. 36. He denied a suggestion that the accident was caused by a tractor whose number he was not able to note down. 37. He deposed that he is an employee of DDA and some of the bills were reimbursed by the department but other bills original thereof are on record were not submitted by him with his department for reimbursement. PW1 stated that claimant is still undergoing treatment and as he is not entitled for reimbursement of regular treatment from his department, he had not taken the bills from doctor/dietitian. 39. He denied a suggestion that claimant does not need any further treatment. 40. Other suggestions contrary to the case of claimant were denied. 41. Second witness examined on behalf of petitioner was Dr. Rishi Nayar, Assistant Professor, Department of Neurology of Dr. R.M.L. Hospital as PW2. 42.
texts.arguments: He deposed in his evidence that he was a member of the Medical Board which had examined the petitioner and proved certificate given to the petitioner as Ex. P1. 43. He deposed that claimant requires self cathetorisation due to constriction of urinary passage as a result of urethral injuries. There are chances that for the rest of his life he may have to use a catheter. However, he could not comment with regard to impotency or otherwise of the petitioner. 44. PW2 also deposed that petitioner will not be able to qualify in physical standards for jobs in army and paramilitary services though he may not suffer any disability for ministerial jobs. 45. In cross examination PW2 deposed that condition of claimant is not likely to improve in a period of six months or year in future. He rather deposed that claimant is suffering from this disability for more than three years now. 46. No other witness was examined by petitioner and no witness was examined by any of the respondents. 59. In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case. 60 . In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. MAC APP. No. 375/06 dated 05.07.12, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held as under: "8. In Bimla Devi and Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009) 13 SC 530, the Supreme Court held that in a petition under Section 166 of the Act, the Claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition under the Motor Vehicles Act. Para 15 of the report is extracted hereunder: "15. It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied." The report in Bimla Devi (Supra) was relied on by the Supreme Court in its latest judgments in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646." 61. In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors.: 2009 ACJ 287, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondentsclaimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal (Supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver." 62. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. It was noted that there is nothing on record to show that the claimant had any enmity with the driver of offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case. In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims: (i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. (ii) Compensation payable in injury cases
